clue.text: One from a happy family, perhaps, is a quick-witted cheat

parts.words: One from a happy family, perhaps
parts.note: Happy Families is a children's card game, so one of it is a card
sharp means clever and alert

explanation.surface: A member of a contented household turns out to be a clever swindler.
explanation.walkthrough: Happy Families is a British children's card game of collecting family sets, which turns 'happy family' into a pack of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardsharp is a swindler who wins by cheating at cards, so a cheat.

clue.text: Spoil beer, dropping old pennies in it

indicators.note: the pennies are dropped into the drink, ending up inside it

parts.note: ale is a beer
d was the symbol for the pre-decimal British penny, so two pennies are DD

explanation.surface: Coins dropped into a pint ruin the beer.
explanation.walkthrough: d, from Latin denarius, stood for a penny before British decimalisation in 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: To addle is to muddle or spoil, as an addled egg has gone bad.

clue.text: An obsession about a couple of lines in the paper

indicators.note: the obsession word is placed about the lines, enclosing them

parts.note: a mania is an obsessive enthusiasm
L stands for line, so two are LL

explanation.surface: Someone is fixated on a brief newspaper mention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The paper' looks like a newspaper, but it is the stuff itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Manilla is a strong brownish paper, used for envelopes and folders, originally made from Manila hemp.

clue.text: Footwear accessories: an advantage to have spikes

parts.note: boot is an old word for advantage or profit, as in 'to boot'
to spike a drink is to lace it with alcohol

explanation.surface: Advice to a runner that spiked shoes give an edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spikes' suggests running shoes, but here it is the verb: spikes a drink, laces it.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the cords threaded through eyelets to fasten shoes and boots, so they accompany footwear.

clue.text: Ostentatiously display a coat of arms

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to proclaim or show off conspicuously
second meaning: a heraldic shield or armorial bearings

explanation.surface: Someone proudly shows off a family coat of arms.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to trumpet or flaunt; the noun is the heraldic term for arms emblazoned on a shield.

clue.text: Remains in place longer than unsuitable corsetry

parts.note: out can mean not acceptable, as in out of the question
stays are the stiffened bones of a corset, or a corset itself

explanation.surface: Ill-fitting corsets are worn long past their welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: Stays is an old name for a corset; out here means not on, unacceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstay is to remain beyond a given limit, as when a guest outstays their welcome.

clue.text: Unconventional call to imbibe drink of milk

indicators.note: to imbibe is to take a drink inside, so one word swallows the other
unconventional means not in the usual form, so these letters break from their normal order

parts.note: taken as written
tea is a drink

explanation.surface: An odd suggestion to drink a glass of milk.
explanation.walkthrough: CALL is rearranged as LACL, which then takes in TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacteal is the adjective relating to milk, from Latin lac, lactis, also used of lymph vessels.

clue.text: Chatted with head of conservatory about wonderful patch of flowers

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter
on means about, as in a talk on a subject
fab is slang for fabulous
a flower bed

explanation.surface: Someone talks with the head gardener about a gorgeous flower bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' sits among the pieces as ON, not as a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To confab is to have an informal talk, short for confabulate, so confabbed means chatted.

clue.text: Character impression

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a distinctive kind or quality
second meaning: a mark pressed into a surface

explanation.walkthrough: Both words look like personality terms; only the first is.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names both a distinguishing type or quality and the imprint left by a die or seal.

clue.text: Left-wing worker about to ask for money, being out of a job

indicators.note: the worker word is wrapped around the asking-for-money word, as one thing sits about another

parts.note: red is the colour of the political left
the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker
to dun is to press a debtor for payment

explanation.surface: A socialist labourer, now jobless, is reduced to begging for cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worker' in crosswords is very often an ant or bee; here the insect does the wrapping, not the left-winger.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker made redundant has lost the post because it is no longer needed, so is jobless.

clue.text: Latin American party line is against the state

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
GA is the postal abbreviation for Georgia, a US state

explanation.surface: A political party's official line is hostile to the government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party line' sounds like policy, but it is a line of dancers at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: The conga is a Cuban dance in which partygoers form a single-file chain, so a line of revellers.

clue.text: Suggests hard work (with which Nightingale was well acquainted)

parts.note: plain reading: a phrase for writing that shows the effort of late-night study

parts.words: with which Nightingale was well acquainted
parts.note: Florence Nightingale was the Lady with the Lamp, so she knew that light intimately

explanation.surface: Florence Nightingale is praised as no stranger to toil.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom describes laboured writing, as if studied by lamplight; the bracket adds the joke that the Lady with the Lamp would know that odour.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom says a piece of writing betrays laborious, burning-the-midnight-oil study rather than easy inspiration.

clue.text: A writer holding a degree resident in the jungle?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the writing tool holds the degree inside it, as a hand holds something

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
MA is a Master of Arts

explanation.surface: A graduate author has gone to live in the jungle.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a loose, playful definition: Tarzan is the jungle's best-known resident.
explanation.definitionFit: An ape-man is a Tarzan-like figure raised among apes, a jungle dweller in fiction.

clue.text: Translated rune with notes without telling others

indicators.note: translated means rendered in another form, so these letters are carried into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A runic inscription with annotations is deciphered in secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Translated' fits the French answer, but here it only reorders letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means between ourselves, said of something kept confidential from outsiders.

clue.text: List of courses finally changed to show this course

indicators.note: finally points at the closing letter, and changed says that letter is swapped for another

parts.note: a syllabus lists the subjects or courses of study

explanation.surface: A college course catalogue is revised to include one more course.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the last letter changes, S becoming B. 'Course' switches from a course of study to a course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Syllabub is a whipped cream dessert, served as the pudding course of a meal.

clue.text: Poor people, we hear, raised family

definitions.note: the answer names the queue or level of the poor rather than the people

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken form, so the spelling may differ from the sound

parts.note: raised, as children or animals are bred
a family line is a lineage

explanation.surface: Impoverished people, rumour says, brought up a family.
explanation.walkthrough: The breadline was originally a queue of the needy waiting for free bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A breadline is a queue of the destitute for food, and living on it means subsisting in poverty.

clue.text: Boxed set of cards (antique)

parts.note: a pack of cards
aged means old

explanation.surface: A boxed deck of playing cards, old enough to be an antique.
explanation.definitionFit: Something packaged has been wrapped or put into a box or container for sale.

clue.text: Two girls, responsibility at first of a joint guardian

parts.note: Pat is a girl's name
Ella is a second girl's name

indicators.note: at first keeps only the opening letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: Two young women share responsibility for a guardian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint guardian' sounds like a shared legal guardian, but the joint is the knee, which the kneecap guards.
explanation.definitionFit: Patellar is the adjective for the patella, the kneecap, the bone shielding the front of the knee.

clue.text: His love could be seen as her love

definitions.text: His love could be seen as her love

parts.words: His love could be seen as her love
parts.note: plain reading: a man's sweetheart might be taken for another woman's
setter's reading: HER plus O, love as zero, spells Hero, the priestess of Greek myth, so the man is her lover

explanation.surface: A tangled romance where his sweetheart might be mistaken for hers.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Greek myth Leander swam the Hellespont each night to his love Hero; HER + O (love, zero) spells her name.
explanation.definitionFit: Leander was the young man who loved Hero, so he is the one whose beloved reads as her-plus-zero.

clue.text: Be a slow mover — walk like a duck, half twisted round

indicators.note: one half of the duck's gait word is turned round to face the other way

parts.note: a duck waddles

explanation.surface: A slow walker is mocked for waddling like a duck, turning half round.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first half of the duck's gait is turned; the second half stays as it was.
explanation.definitionFit: To dawdle is to move idly and slowly, lingering and wasting time on the way.

clue.text: Porter and doctor in charge of old distilling apparatus

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, so an ale
MB is a Bachelor of Medicine
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A hospital porter and a doctor are put in charge of an old still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' looks like the hospital worker beside the doctor, but it is the dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: An alembic is the gourd-shaped vessel with a beaked head used by alchemists for distillation.

clue.text: A very loud indication of trouble

parts.note: taken as written
ff, fortissimo, is the musical mark for very loud
a ray is a glimmer or sign, as in a ray of hope

explanation.surface: A loud noise warns that trouble is brewing.
explanation.definitionFit: An affray is a public brawl or disturbance of the peace, a breach that causes trouble.

clue.text: A remote place: North Dakota, perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: somewhere far from anywhere
second meaning, read literally: ND, its abbreviation, is the last two letters of a word

explanation.surface: North Dakota is mocked as somewhere in the middle of nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: North Dakota looks like an example of a remote place, but its abbreviation ND forms the rear of the word BEYOND.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for an isolated spot far from towns, and literally names the ending letters of beyond.

clue.text: Bone up excellent piece

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters run from the bottom upwards

parts.note: A1, first-rate, with the 1 written as I
a bit is a piece

explanation.surface: Swot up on a fine piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bone up' reads as one phrase meaning study, but the definition is just 'Bone'.
explanation.definitionFit: The tibia is the shinbone, the larger of the two bones of the lower leg.

clue.text: Frustrated fellow removed drunk

indicators.note: removed tells us the fellow abbreviation is taken away from the other word

parts.note: to foil a plan is to frustrate it
F is the abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: A thwarted man was thrown out for being drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: F is taken from the front of FOILED. Well oiled is slang for tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Oiled is informal slang for intoxicated, from the idiom well-oiled meaning drunk.

clue.text: Royal descent of one after the Crown Jewels?

definitions.note: names the lineage; the answer is the word in 'royal blood'
definitions.meaning: first meaning: to be of royal lineage is to have royal ...
second meaning: Colonel Thomas ... tried to steal the Crown Jewels from the Tower of London in 1671

explanation.surface: A royal heir's line of succession seems to come after the Crown Jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' looks like order of succession but means chasing: Colonel Blood was the Irish adventurer who tried to steal the Crown Jewels in 1671.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood means lineage or ancestry, as in royal blood, and Colonel Blood was the would-be jewel thief.

clue.text: Gay Parisienne sporting obscene loose blouse

indicators.note: someone sporting a garment wears it around them, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: gai is French for cheerful, the word a Parisian would use
ribald means coarse or indecent

explanation.surface: A merry Paris woman wears a risqué, loose-fitting top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parisienne' asks for the French word. A garibaldi is a loose red blouse modelled on the shirts of Garibaldi's soldiers; in Britain it is also a currant biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A garibaldi is a loose-fitting blouse, once fashionable for women, copied from the red shirts of Garibaldi's followers.

clue.text: Scrum of RU lads, yes? Yes!

indicators.note: a scrum is a heaving, jumbled pack of bodies, so the letters are churned into a new order

parts.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: Rugby union players in a scrum are asked if they are ready, and shout back yes.
explanation.walkthrough: RU is Rugby Union, the code in which scrums are a set piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Assuredly is an emphatic adverb of agreement meaning certainly, so it can stand in for an exclaimed yes.

clue.text: Act as solicitor for defendant initially in prison?

indicators.note: the selected letter is placed in the prison word, locked inside it

parts.note: a cage is a place of confinement

indicators.note: initially keeps just the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: A lawyer acts for the accused who is in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' looks like the British lawyer, but it is someone who solicits, that is, begs.
explanation.definitionFit: To cadge is to beg or scrounge, and a solicitor in the old sense is one who asks for things.
